- **P4 = Public-Private-People Partnership** (also written **People–Private–Public Partnership for the Poor**); launched by CM Naidu and Dy CM Pawan Kalyan at **Velagapudi, Amaravati** on **Ugadi, 30 March 2025** (a Sunday) – not Independence Day, Republic Day or Diwali; rolled out statewide from **19 August 2025**.
- **Goal:** complete eradication of poverty (**Zero Poverty** – the first Padi Sutram of Swarna Andhra @2047); linked with **SDG 1 (No Poverty)**; under the **Planning Department** – the **Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation** works for poverty eradication.
- **Model:** the **top 10%** of society adopt the **bottom 20%**; a whole-of-society, **voluntary** model in which government is only a **facilitator** (claimed as a **first-of-its-kind convergence model**); voluntary help (aid, mentoring) – **not a cash-transfer scheme**.
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Margadarsi / Margadarshi | well-off mentor or donor who adopts a family – individuals, NGOs or corporates; a **volunteer** (not nominated by government); gives emotional reassurance, guidance and continuous support beyond money |
| Bangaru Kutumbam / Bangaru Kutumbalu | "Golden Families": the poor beneficiary families who are adopted |
| Level | P4 head |
|---|---|
| State society | Chairperson CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; Vice-Chairperson Dy CM Pawan Kalyan; CEO, Director, call centre |
| District | District In-charge Ministers |
| Constituency | MLAs |
| Village/ward | Panchayat / Ward Administrative Secretaries |
- Donor platforms **Milaap, DonateKart, RangDe**; **Dokka Seethamma** (19th-century social reformer known for selfless service to the poor) is remembered in P4 messaging.
- **Scale:** first target **5 lakh** Golden Families adopted by **15 August 2025** (Phase 1 scale about **21.8 lakh families**); about **19.16 lakh** Bangaru families identified.
- **First anniversary (30 Mar 2026, Sri Padmavati Mahila Viswa Vidyalayam, Tirupati):** **1.06 lakh Margadarsis** had adopted about **10.3 lakh families**; companies adopted **8,904 families in Kuppam** under CSR (about **9,000** by **Adani, TVS Motor and MEIL**, Jul 2026); goal restated as a **poverty-free society by 2047** (revised from zero poverty by 2029).
> Margadarsi = mentor (adopts); Bangaru Kutumbam = poor family (adopted). Primary goal of P4 = poverty eradication (SDG 1).

- **Kovind High-Level Committee:** set up **2 September 2023**; report to **President Droupadi Murmu** on **14 March 2024** (**18,626 pages**); proposed **Article 82A** (synchronise terms of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies) and **Article 324A** (municipal and panchayat polls with general elections).
- Lok Sabha and Assembly polls first, local-body polls **within 100 days**; the amendment for Art. 82A needs **no State ratification**.

- **Equal Opportunity Centre (EOC)** - nodal body in **every HEI**; **Equity Committees** chaired by the **head of the institution** (SC, ST, OBC, women, PwD representation), meeting **at least twice a year**; the head is **personally responsible**; a **national monitoring committee** of UGC.

- **24/7 grievance system** - helplines, portals, **Equity Officers, Equity Squads**; bi-annual public reports; annual compliance report to UGC. Penalties: debarment from UGC schemes, bar on degree/online/distance programmes, removal from the UGC list.

- Notified to **replace the 2012 regulations**; caste discrimination defined as against **SC, ST, OBC** (OBCs were excluded only in the draft) – aligned with **Articles 15(4), 15(5)**; the draft's **fine for "false complaints"** was dropped – **no explicit penalty for false complaints**.
- Gaps: no explicit admission-stage discrimination; the 2012 ban on "**separate educational systems**" removed. Evidence cited: **IIT Delhi (2019)** – 75% of marginalised students faced discrimination; **Thorat Committee (2007)**.

- Subsidies: **cash transfers 20.2%** of subsidy spend (2025–26) vs **3%** (2018–19).

- **Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025** (Ministry of Education): introduced **15 December 2025**; a **single apex body** to replace **UGC, AICTE, NCTE** and other regulators, with **Regulatory, Standards and Accreditation Councils** (10 Jul 2026).

fix.s: The third- and fourth-child cash and millet incentives that AP's Collectors' Conference (May 2026) expected to start on 15 August 2026 were actually launched, as Pillale Sampada, on which date?
fix.x: They were launched earlier than expected: CM Chandrababu Naidu launched Pillale Sampada (₹30,000 for a third child, ₹40,000 for a fourth) in Vijayawada on World Population Day, 11 July 2026. 15 August 2026 was only the start date expected in May; 7–8 May 2026 was the Collectors' Conference.
